title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JADA'S CLIMB
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Jada Simmons, a gas station cashier in Bloomington, Illinois.
Jada got dizzy on a step stool.
So naturally, she decided to climb wind turbines for a living.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE FLYER
segments.author: Terence
lines: One slow night, she saw a flyer. Wind technician training. Double the pay.
She laughed. Then she remembered Grandpa Otis, an old crop-duster pilot.
Over his hangar door, he had painted a line from Terence, an ancient Roman writer:
Fortune favors the brave.
Jada tore off the phone number before she could change her mind.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PRACTICE TOWER
segments.quote: It is possible to fly without motors, but not without knowledge and skill.
segments.author: Wilbur Wright
lines: Day one, the practice ladder was forty feet. Jada froze at ten.
The instructor, Ray, pointed at a framed line from Wilbur Wright:
It is possible to fly without motors, but not without knowledge and skill.
So she learned the gear. Harness. Two hooks. Three points of contact.
Fear got smaller as the checklist got longer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE RESCUE TEST
segments.quote: Always bear in mind that your own resolution to succeed is more important than any other one thing.
segments.author: Abraham Lincoln
lines: Then came the rescue test. She lowered the dummy, Dave, way too slow. Failed.
She cried in her Corolla. Her mom texted a photo of the Lincoln magnet on their fridge:
Always bear in mind that your own resolution to succeed is more important than any other one thing.
She practiced every lunch break. Two weeks later, she passed. Dave was fine.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THREE HUNDRED FEET
segments.quote: I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it.
segments.author: Nelson Mandela
lines: Her first real turbine was three hundred feet tall. Her hands shook.
Her partner Earl, twenty-two years on towers, said, Me too. Every time.
Then he quoted Nelson Mandela:
I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it.
Jada clipped in and took one rung. Then the next. All the way up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LOGBOOK
segments.quote: One never notices what has been done; one can only see what remains to be done.
segments.author: Marie Curie
lines: By winter, she felt slow. Her list of can'ts kept growing.
Earl tossed her the logbook. Forty-one climbs. Then he read her a line from Marie Curie:
One never notices what has been done; one can only see what remains to be done.
So Jada counted climbs, not mistakes. Then she started training the new guy.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE VIEW
segments.quote: In every walk with nature one receives far more than he seeks.
segments.author: John Muir
lines: One spring morning, she stood on top of a turbine. Cornfields forever. A hawk below her feet.
She called her mom from up there. Her mom screamed. The good kind.
She thought of John Muir, the nature writer:
In every walk with nature one receives far more than he seeks.
She came for a paycheck. She got the sky.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be brave. Learn the skill. Keep going. Feel the fear. Count your wins. Look around.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Be brave. Learn the skill. Keep going. Feel the fear and climb. Count your wins. Look around.
I climbed a ladder once to change a light bulb. I'm still recovering.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
